input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 conditions our freedom to source elsewhere: we may not engage another provider until we have disclosed a competing offer to Vendor and matched it for Vendor, which is a right of first refusal operating as de facto exclusivity binding Customer. It fails the fallback on every material term — no defined product category, no 12-month outer limit, and no automatic end on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates — and, running for the full three-year term with no performance-based exit, it sits in walk-away territory. Section 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges no exclusivity commitment) points the right way but is contradicted by the operative gating obligation in Section 7.2, so the restriction must be removed rather than left to interpretation. The related MFN/price-matching aspect is addressed here through the same deletion and is not flagged again. Section 2.1 (take-or-pay minimum) and Section 12.4 (non-compete) are separate commercial terms for their own rules.

ops.oldText: Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
ops.newText: Customer may engage any other provider at any time and has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation to Vendor.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the requirement to disclose and match third-party offers before engaging another provider, because it operates as a right of first refusal and de facto exclusivity on us, and replaced it with confirmation that we have no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation, consistent with Section 12.3.
proposal.summary: Replace the disclose-and-match precondition in Section 7.2 with an express no-exclusivity statement.

mappings.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
